newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea plans foreign ownership in Korea Telecom.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea plans foreign ownership in Korea Telecom.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Tuesday it planned to allow foreign ownership in state-run Korea Telecom of 20 percent from 1998 and 33 percent from 2001.
A ministry statement said it would limit individual foreign shareholdings in Korea Telecom to three percent.
The ministry said it aimed to submit to parliament a draft of a special regulation in early June to privatise four state-run companies.
The four companies are Korea Telecom, Korea Gas Corp, Korea Tobacco and Ginseng Corp and Korea Heavy Industries and Construction Corp.
The ministry said it would privatise the four by selling their stakes and introducing professional managers.
It said individuals' shares in the four firms initially would be limited to five percent and later raised to a maximum of 10 percent.
